findings: SWR-025 in workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md is not objectively verifiable as written: it applies to an unspecified 'ready-flag query' and its verification uses 'measure execution' and 'returns 0U immediately' without an objective measurement method, threshold, or defined way to observe that only a single read occurs.

SWR-026 in workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md is not atomic and not objectively verifiable as written: it covers any 'named RCC register bit' without naming a register, bit, or function, and its verification refers to 'the target RCC register' and 'the named bit' as placeholders, so a single test cannot objectively verify the requirement.

SWR-024 in workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md is not objectively verified by the stated robot test: comparing read-back RCC register values against reset defaults cannot detect a write that leaves the register value equal to the reset default, so the test cannot objectively verify 'shall not write any RCC register'.

The verification texts in workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md are inconsistent about the register-block array index required by .forge-run/manifest.json#scope-target-budgets: SWR-001/002 use LL_RCC_CR_OFFSET/4U, SWR-003/004 use LL_RCC_RCC_CR_OFFSET/4U, SWR-014-019 use LL_RCC_RCC_AHB1ENR_OFFSET/4U, and SWR-020-023 use ll_rcc_regs[RCC_AHB1RSTR], leaving the exact element to initialize and check undefined.

SWR-010, SWR-011, SWR-012, and SWR-013 in workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md use field-like access on an array element such as ll_rcc_regs[RCC_SR].HSIRDY, which is inconsistent with ll_rcc_regs being a register-block array and does not specify the generated offset or bit position to set and check, so the verification is not objectively executable as written.

SWR-001, SWR-002, SWR-003, and SWR-004 in workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md have verification steps that do not objectively verify preservation of all other RCC_CR bits: the tests initialize the other RCC_CR bits to 0 and would still pass if the function cleared or corrupted other bits that were initially set.

CPU constraint missing: workproducts/SWE.1/software_requirements.md and .forge-run/manifest.json#scope-target-budgets define measurable flash, static-RAM, and stack limits, but they do not state an explicit measurable CPU/cycle constraint for the RCC LL public API calls (SWR-001 through SWR-026).
